title: Story bible for The Last Signal (auto-populated)
message: Get the story bible for "The Last Signal"

entries.name: Crane
entries.description: Administrator and de facto warlord controlling a network of at least three settlements. Methodical, unsentimental leader who manages people through leverage, protection arrangements, and careful intelligence-gathering. Keeps a detailed ledger tracking assets and risks. Has a persistent headache and ache between his shoulders. Has operated his network for at least four years.

entries.name: Dov
entries.description: A person known to Mara, encountered approximately six months before the chapter's events. Traded four D-cells for company and did not press Mara about a previous ambiguous carrier-wave signal. Relationship and location not specified beyond proximity.

entries.name: Pollard
entries.description: Crane's second-in-command, approximately forty years old, looks fifty. Described as completely without sentiment. Habitually stands with his back to walls, eyes moving in a fixed pattern: gate, shed, table, gate. Wears a canvas jacket with collar turned up. Clean, re-soled boots. Sent as envoy when Crane wants the other party to feel they had a choice. Skilled at cataloguing assets rather than exits.

entries.name: Foss
entries.description: A trader operating out of or through the Ridgeline market. Known to talk too much. Spread word of Mara's signal detection, leading Sable to Settlement Seven.

entries.name: Mara Voss
entries.description: Radio engineer, pre-collapse trained. Lives and works at Settlement Seven. Independent operator with no faction affiliation. Trades technical repairs for food and components. Has been tracking a repeating shortwave signal for at least four nights. Keeps a water-damaged frequency notebook. Resourceful, methodical, writes things down and measures intervals. Flagged in Crane's ledger as a watch-not-act risk. Decides to travel to Station Halcyon by end of chapter.

entries.name: Hendricks
entries.description: One of Crane's scouts. Writes reports in cramped hand on the back of old invoice sheets. Underlines words twice to indicate personal confirmation rather than inference. Observed Mara Voss for two months. Added a personal postscript noting Mara was smiling when she wrote down her findings.

entries.name: Sable
entries.description: Crale's advance lieutenant. Moves ahead of Crale's main force as a rapid-deployment unit. Described as moving the way a hand moves ahead of a body reaching for something. Believed to be the source of the dust signature eight miles east of Mara and Tomás's camp, suggesting Mara and Tomás were noted at the Ridgeway checkpoint and reported.

entries.name: Yael
entries.description: Physician at Settlement Seven, ER-trained. Has been at the settlement at least seven years. Supplies antibiotics, analgesics, and a confirmed insulin cache. Has a monthly delivery arrangement with Crane in exchange for protection designation and non-interference. Has been providing background intelligence on Mara to one of Crane's supply runners for fourteen months in exchange for medicine. Keeps names of four children she has delivered in her coat pocket. Warns Mara about Pollard's visit and urges her to flee. Has two current critical patients: a pregnant woman three months from term with two prior losses, and a boy named Dov with a recurring chest infection.

entries.name: Holt
entries.description: Senior engineer on the FEMA Emergency Broadcast Protocol working group. Wore gray hair in a flat-top, drank black coffee, had thirty years in emergency communications. Overruled Mara on the five-tone confirmation sequence. Coined the phrase 'Redundancy is not waste.' Presumed dead by Mara. His design choices are central to Mara recognizing the signal.

entries.name: Garrett (or Garrety)
entries.description: FEMA officer on the Kansas City working group. Argued for MGRS coordinate format on grounds of military standardization. Lost the argument to Mara, who advocated for lat-long. Fate unknown. Gender: female.

entries.name: Mara
entries.description: Protagonist. Skilled radio operator and signal decoder. Carries a rebuilt shortwave receiver and improvised aerial. Has been tracking a structured multi-layer transmission for at least several days. Practical, calculating, guarded with information even from allies. Has carried her receiver for four years. Experienced survivor navigating post-Pulse wasteland.

entries.name: Tomás
entries.description: Mara's guide and travelling companion. Hired for navigation through dangerous territory; rate renegotiated when true destination proved forty miles deeper into Crale's territory than originally disclosed. Experienced pathfinder with knowledge of Crale's patrol patterns. Has claustrophobia or trauma response to enclosed spaces. Calm, methodical, perceptive; handles objects when thinking. Carries pre-collapse binoculars with cracked rubber eyecups.

entries.name: Fen
entries.description: Checkpoint enforcer for the Ridgeway Compact. Woman of Mara's age or slightly older, with a strong jaw and professional scanning eyes. Wears heavily repaired military surplus jacket with a hand-stitched Ridgeway Compact patch on the left shoulder. Confiscated Mara's shortwave receiver under a licensing ordinance used effectively as confiscation. Unknowingly returned the most critical component—the loading coil—by handing back the telescoping antenna. Not malicious but unsentimental.

entries.name: Crale
entries.description: Regional warlord or faction leader whose territory lies southwest of the story's opening. Controls the interior region where the bunker is located. Runs mobile sweep patrols rather than fixed checkpoints in his core territory. Has supply corridors crossing the route to the bunker. Controlling the seed vault would give him significant power.

entries.name: Station Halcyon beacon protocol
entries.description: The facility was designed to broadcast on 6.925 MHz if it went to emergency autonomous operation. The beacon was to run until someone came to shut it off or until power failed. Personnel were told it would probably never activate. The signal pulses in an eleven-second rhythm.

entries.name: Station Halcyon secondary access sequence
entries.description: An undocumented field modification made during the second construction rotation. To open the personnel shaft hatch from outside: push the recessed handle on the left side of the hatch frame before turning the main wheel, or the wheel locks. This fix was never formally recorded; official records indicate the wheel alone opens the hatch.

entries.name: Series Bible
entries.description:
SYNOPSIS: Seven years after a solar electromagnetic pulse destroys global infrastructure, a former radio engineer discovers that a repeating signal buried in atmospheric static is not random noise — it is a structured transmission from a pre-collapse government bunker whose occupants believe the outside world is dead. To reach the bunker before a warlord's army does, she must cross 400 miles of fractured wasteland, decode the signal's coordinates, and decide whether the bunker's secret — a cache of seed-vault biotechnology that could restart agriculture — belongs to everyone or only to those with the power to control it.
STORY ARC: The Hero's Journey
TARGET CHAPTER COUNT: 8
DRAMATIC QUESTION: Can radio engineer Mara Voss decode the last signal, reach the buried bunker, and bring its life-saving biotechnology to the wasteland's survivors before the warlord Crale seizes it and uses it to enslave them?

entries.name: The Pulse
entries.description: The catastrophic event approximately seven years before the story's present that collapsed modern infrastructure and civilisation. Caused the end of reliable power, communications, and supply chains. Led to the rise of faction territories, scavenger economies, and the loss of agricultural diversity. Nature of the event not specified in this chapter.

entries.name: FEMA Emergency Broadcast Protocol (EBP)
entries.description: A communications protocol drafted by a working group including Mara and Holt in Kansas City, produced as a 47-page specification. Core feature: a framing sequence of three attention tones, a four-second pause, and five confirmation tones, designed to survive degraded channels. Never fully deployed before the Pulse. The incoming signal uses this exact framing sequence, which Mara recognizes as her own work.

entries.name: Annex C-7 / Power-Constrained Coordinate Transmission
entries.description: A sub-section of the FECC Comms Annex C specifying that operators transmitting below 15% rated power may use abbreviated coordinates (degrees only, cardinal direction, no decimal extension). The receiving station is expected to acknowledge and request refinement. The incoming signal uses this format, indicating the sender is severely power-constrained.

entries.name: Timing diagram
entries.description: A signal-analysis method Mara developed in her first year of listening. She draws a horizontal line marked in one-second intervals and places received tones as vertical bars above it. Originally developed to decode ghost signals from resonating broadcast towers; now used to analyze the incoming transmission and confirm its structured, non-random character.

entries.name: Skywave / ionospheric propagation
entries.description: The HF radio propagation mechanism Mara relies on and understands deeply. Signals bounce off the ionosphere's F-layer and return to earth hundreds or thousands of miles away. Solar flux, atmospheric conditions, and time of day affect propagation paths. Mara uses propagation character to estimate solar flux index and to evaluate whether a signal could be an atmospheric reflection of a pre-collapse broadcast.

entries.name: The Multi-Layer Transmission Protocol
entries.description: A deliberate, structured contact protocol broadcast from the bunker. Consists of at least three layers: Layer 1 is a broadcast position giving a general area grid. Layer 2 refines to precise coordinates, encoded so that Layer 1 is required to decrypt it. Layer 3 is a time-indexed countdown sequence indicating the bunker's power-failure deadline. Each layer is received in separate transmission windows. Designed to resist interception—only someone with the right equipment and all prior layers can extract the true location.

entries.name: The Nine-Day Countdown
entries.description: The bunker's backup power—running for seven years since the Pulse—will fail in nine days from the story's present (originally eleven days from the first transmission Mara received, two days ago). When power fails, transmissions stop, ventilation stops, and anyone inside dies. Drives the urgency of Mara and Tomás's journey.

entries.name: First signal transmission
entries.description: Received by Mara at approximately 05:47 on the chapter's morning. Frequency: 7.200 MHz (later logged as 7.455 MHz in second transmission context—noted as possible logging detail). Content: FEMA EBP framing sequence (three tones, four-second pause, five tones) followed by eleven seconds of corrupted Morse. Mara decodes four candidate characters: F, E, ?, A (middle character possibly K or D). Interpreted as a partial grid fragment.

entries.name: Kansas City working group sessions
entries.description: Four meetings over eight months in a federal building in Kansas City, pre-Pulse. Produced the 47-page FEMA Emergency Broadcast Protocol specification and the FECC Comms Annex C. Attendees included Mara, Holt, the unnamed lawyer, three engineers, and a FEMA regional coordinator who attended only the first and last sessions. Key decisions: five-tone confirmation retained over Mara's objection; lat-long format adopted over MGRS at Mara's advocacy.

entries.name: Second signal transmission
entries.description: Received by Mara approximately 41 minutes after the first, on 7.455 MHz. Stronger signal, cleaner Morse. Content: same FEMA EBP framing sequence followed by nine seconds of Morse yielding six unambiguous characters: 3, 8, N, 1, 0, 4. Decoded as abbreviated coordinates 38 North, 104 West per Annex C-7 format. Confirms the sender is power-constrained and following the FECC protocol.

entries.name: Confiscation of the Receiver at the Ridgeway Checkpoint
entries.description: Fen seized Mara's shortwave receiver under a Ridgeway Compact licensing ordinance and locked it in the holding cage. She then returned the telescoping antenna to Mara, not knowing it contained the loading coil—the most critical component. This event forced Mara to build an improvised aerial and is the inciting action of the chapter's central problem.

entries.name: Detection of the Pursuing Dust Signature
entries.description: From their creek-bed camp, Tomás spotted a dust signature eight miles east, consistent with four to six people moving fast in formation before making camp. Believed to be Sable's unit. Suggests Mara and Tomás were noted and reported at the Ridgeway checkpoint. Establishes that they are being followed and have approximately one day's lead.

entries.name: Station Halcyon facility schematic
entries.description: An original construction schematic of Station Halcyon kept by Sable as a personal copy. Not yet retrieved at chapter's end; Sable leaves to collect it and will return within an hour. Sable kept it to remember what she built that she wasn't proud of.

entries.name: The broadcast console / receiver
entries.description: Mara's primary radio equipment. Originally a production-room broadcast board from a regional AM station, found in pieces in Abilene and rebuilt by Mara over eleven days using a soldering iron run off a car battery. Front panel buckled on the left; two fader knobs replaced with hand-whittled wooden dowels. The receiver section is fully functional. Central to all of Mara's signal work.

entries.name: Realistic DX-394
entries.description: Shortwave receiver scavenged from a ham operator's estate. The ham died in the second winter; his widow traded it for two months of firewood before understanding its value. Mara carried it forty miles on her back and has maintained it ever since. Known quirks: squelch control sticks at low end, slight digital readout drift corrected by ear, AGC circuit pumps on strong static bursts.

entries.name: FECC Comms Annex C (draft document)
entries.description: Internal FEMA document titled 'FECC Comms Annex C: Degraded-Environment Transmission Standards.' Stamped DRAFT, NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION. Page 31, Annex C-7 covers coordinate transmission under power-constrained conditions (below 15% rated output), authorizing abbreviated degrees-only format. Mara has a copy stored on her shelf. Key to her interpretation of the signal.

entries.name: Long-wire antenna
entries.description: Mara's HF antenna, strung from the water tower's crown to a fence post forty meters away. Height clears ground-level interference. Requires periodic maintenance of connections. A bird landing on it produces a faint elastic twang. A loose guy-wire taps the exterior boards in wind.

entries.name: Marantz cassette deck
entries.description: Battered cassette recorder hardwired into the receiver's output, running off a separate battery. Used by Mara to record and play back transmissions for analysis. Loaded with a tape she has been using, erasing, and reusing for two years.

entries.name: The Improvised Aerial
entries.description: Field-built antenna constructed by Mara at the gas station from: twelve feet of two-conductor copper wire, the telescoping antenna with its loading coil, sheet-metal clamps made from a collapsed display rack, two steel screws from a junction box, insulated three-conductor cable stripped from a wall, and a rebar ground stake. Approximately sixteen feet of conductor total. Electrically correct despite crude appearance. Paired with a salvaged earbud as detector. Successfully received the second and third transmission layers.

entries.name: The Ridgeway Compact Holding Cage
entries.description: A livestock crate retrofitted with a newer padlock, bolted to the inside of the overpass guardrail. Contains confiscated equipment including a solar lantern, a hand-crank torch, a CB radio with its antenna snapped off, and Mara's receiver. Described by Mara as a graveyard; items are effectively never returned.

entries.name: The Telescoping Antenna
entries.description: Eight-section telescoping aluminium antenna from Mara's confiscated receiver. Returned to Mara by Fen, who did not know its significance. The base section contains a loading coil—the most critical component—which Fen unknowingly handed back. Fully extended, approximately four feet. Used as the core of Mara's improvised aerial.

entries.name: Settlement Seven
entries.description: One of at least three settlements in Crane's network. Location of Mara Voss's workshop and Yael's medical practice. Has a main yard, supply shed, rationing table, and a fence with a gap. Referenced in relation to settlements Eight and others.

entries.name: Station Halcyon
entries.description: Continuity-of-government facility, informal name not appearing on official paperwork. Located approximately at grid reference 47.3N / 110.8W, roughly four hundred miles from Settlement Seven. Built with hardened power systems: dedicated diesel tanks, shielded generators, independent UPS systems. Has a main vehicle ramp with blast door and a concealed secondary personnel shaft. Broadcasting a repeating beacon on 6.925 MHz since at least the collapse. Designed to survive EMP and operate autonomously.

entries.name: Ridgeline market
entries.description: A trade market location where Sable passed through three days before arriving at Settlement Seven. Trader Foss was present there and spoke about Mara's signal detection.

entries.name: Eastern corridor
entries.description: A geographic and political zone controlled by Crane as far as a river. Beyond the river is open faction territory with at least three unpredictable groups. The route Mara must travel to reach Station Halcyon.

entries.name: Crale
entries.description: A named faction or settlement whose nearest outpost is far enough from Garfield that no one passes through without purpose. Mara chose Garfield partly to avoid Crale's presence. Nature and threat level not yet specified, but treated as a danger to be avoided.

entries.name: Garfield
entries.description: Small pre-collapse town, population 812 per a recovered sign. Located on elevated ground above surrounding plain, chosen by Mara for its emptiness, antenna height advantage, and distance from Crale's nearest settlement. Main Street storefronts are collapsed. Streets retain their grid geometry despite freeze-thaw damage.

entries.name: The water tower
entries.description: Mara's home and radio station. A decommissioned municipal water tower in Garfield. Contains an empty 40,000-gallon rust-scoured tank at its base, a reinforced catwalk above where Mara sleeps and works, and a single intact window facing east. Leans three degrees to the northwest. Corrugated panel walls with rag-stuffed gaps.

entries.name: Kansas City (federal building)
entries.description: Location of the FEMA working group conference room where Mara helped draft the Emergency Broadcast Protocol and Annex C-7. Smelled of carpet cleaner and old coffee. Mara left Kansas City in the first week after the Pulse, taking eleven notebooks.

entries.name: Abilene
entries.description: Town where Mara found the broadcast console in pieces across three rooms of a strip mall. She carried it out over four trips, walking four miles each way.

entries.name: Salina, Kansas
entries.description: Location of a public radio affiliate where Mara worked before the Pulse, stripping a broadcast board from a regional AM station during a renovation. Establishes her pre-collapse professional background.

entries.name: 38 North, 104 West (signal origin region)
entries.description: Abbreviated coordinates transmitted in the second signal burst. Places the source in a box roughly 200 miles across straddling the Colorado-Kansas border: high plains, scrubland, eastern edge of the Rockies. Mara estimates it is approximately 400 miles from her location. The unknown transmitter is somewhere within this region.

entries.name: The Seed Vault
entries.description: Located within the bunker. Contains preserved grain varieties and crop diversity representing a biological library capable of restarting agricultural variety lost since the Pulse. Settlements currently survive on a narrow rotation of only the crop varieties that survived in quantity. Controlling the vault would give Crale decisive power. Primary objective of Mara's mission.

entries.name: County Road Junction
entries.description: A crossing point approximately a day and a half southwest of the gas station camp, inside Crale's territory. Site where Tomás previously lost one member of a five-person group to a Crale patrol. Significant waypoint on the route to the bunker.

entries.name: Ridgeway Compact
entries.description: A newly established district authority controlling the overpass checkpoint. Has issued ordinances requiring licenses for any signal-receiving or transmitting equipment crossing district boundaries. Operates a confiscation cage on the overpass. Did not exist six months before the story's present. Ridgeway proper is three days east of the checkpoint.

entries.name: The Overpass Checkpoint
entries.description: A toll checkpoint on a former highway overpass, operated by the Ridgeway Compact. Two rusted pickup trucks nose-to-nose form the barricade. A steel livestock crate retrofitted with a padlock serves as a holding cage for confiscated equipment. Location where Mara's receiver was seized.

entries.name: The Gas Station
entries.description: An abandoned, thoroughly gutted service station where Mara and Tomás camp after the checkpoint. Pumps removed to the base. Canopy still standing with one bent support column. Service bay contains a flooded lift pit and residual salvageable materials. Mara builds her improvised aerial here. Located roughly one day's travel from the overpass.

entries.name: The Collapsed Rail Underpass
entries.description: A rail bridge that partially collapsed over a state highway in the first year after the Pulse. Approximately 200 metres long with clearance crushed to roughly half original height; lowest point around the 100-metre mark requires hands-and-knees crawling. Left-of-centre line is safest due to compacted foot traffic. Passable but psychologically difficult for Tomás. Located on the fastest southwest route.

entries.name: The Bunker
entries.description: A pre-collapse government facility retrofitted after the Pulse, located approximately 260 miles west-southwest of the story's opening, deep inside Crale's core territory. Contains a seed vault with preserved grain varieties and crop diversity critical to post-Pulse agricultural recovery. Has been running on stored backup power for seven years. Power—and with it ventilation and transmissions—will fail in nine days from the story's present. Someone professional is or was inside.

entries.name: Millford Junction
entries.description: Location of a scavenger market two days south of the overpass. Mentioned as a possible source for a replacement receiver. Rejected by Mara as too time-costly.

entries.name: Repeating radio signal
entries.description: - **Repeating radio signal**: In a post-EMP setting, a structured broadcast buried in static would be heard as a *carrier* or *tone* that remains stable while the noise floor shifts, because atmospheric interference and damaged transmitters produce crackle, flutter, and fading around a fixed signal. Radio operators use *direction finding* and pattern recognition to distinguish an intentional transmission from random interference, especially when the message repeats on a schedule or in a coded se

entries.name: Independent factions
entries.description:
- **Checkpoint procedures**: Road checkpoints in fractured wastelands are typically improvised with vehicles, barricades, portable radios, and visible weapons rather than permanent architecture. Confiscated electronics would be treated as leverage or contraband, especially anything that can transmit or receive signals across distance.[4][2]
